feedback.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z={y}^{2}{e}^{2x}-1$ at the point $(0,2,3).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}{e}^{2x}-1) \\  & =2{y}^{2}{e}^{2x} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}{e}^{2x}-1) \\  & =2y{e}^{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(0,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(0,2) & =2(2)^{2}{e}^{2(0)}=8 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(0,2) & =2(2){e}^{2(0)}=4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-3 & =(x-0)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(0,2)+(y-2)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(0,2) \\ z-3 & =8(x-0)+4(y-2) \\ z-3 & =8x+4y-8 \\ -8x-4y+z+5 & =0 \\ 8x+4y-z-5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
